title: Normalize brick/CMU/stone dims; poured concrete != unit masonry
remoteBaseline: main sandbox pull 2026-11-08 (no remote writes; baseline = remote-src/ verbatim snapshot)
summary: Poured/cast concrete walls were never actually priceable, and off-enum subtype spellings silently priced as mortared unit masonry. Remote check() required positive wall_unit_length/width/height on every wall material and isConcrete was a strict === 'concrete' string test: a UI-authored concrete row (the catalog preset wrote 0 length/height) was always held 'unavailable', a concrete row with positive unit dims priced a fictional brick count, and a row authored 'poured_concrete' or 'cmu' was silently classified unit masonry (mortar bags and courses billed on poured concrete). The candidate adds a canonical wall-material subtype classifier at the inventory boundary, makes the subtype pick the quantity method in the wall check, and gives poured concrete a distinct quantity basis: placed volume in cubic yards (outline perimeter x wall height x cataloged wall thickness), with no courses, mortar joints, or per-unit production hours. Catalog surfaces declare the basis honestly: the concrete preset clears (not zeroes) unit length/height and writes unit 'cy', cost labels read $/CY, the BOM and Builder part units follow the snapshot's recorded materialQuantityUnit, and the walls panel labels poured quantity as CY instead of 'Units'. Unit masonry (brick / cinderblock / stone / absent subtype — the legacy default for brick_stone rows) is byte-identical to remote under a 30+ scenario remote-parity control.

subtypeContract.canonicalEnum: WALL_MATERIAL_SUBTYPES = [brick, cinderblock, stone, concrete] — matches the FoundationInventory entity jsonc wall_material_subtype enum exactly. brick/cinderblock/stone = unit masonry (unit-count method); concrete = poured (CY volume method).
subtypeContract.canonicalWallMaterialSubtype(value): trim/lowercase/separator-collapse then FOUNDATION_WALL_MATERIAL_SUBTYPE_ALIASES lookup. Returns enum value, or null when absent/blank (not recorded -> legacy unit-masonry default) or recorded-but-unrecognized (hold, never guessed).
subtypeContract.wallMaterialSubtypeRecorded(value): undefined/null/blank-string = not recorded; anything else (including non-string values) is a recorded classification that must classify or hold.
subtypeContract.aliases: cmu/concrete block/cinder block/block -> cinderblock; natural stone/cut stone/limestone/sandstone/stone veneer -> stone; poured_concrete/poured/poured in place/cast_in_place/cast-in-place/monolithic concrete -> concrete; clay/face/veneer brick -> brick.
subtypeContract.normalization: normalizeFoundationInventoryRow rewrites a resolved subtype to canonical on the calculation copy (idempotent); absent stays absent (no key minted); unrecognized passes through VERBATIM so the wall check holds on the authored value. Authored entity rows are never mutated. Existing field-alias fills (brick_* -> wall_unit_*) unchanged: only absent canonical keys fill, an explicit canonical null still beats the legacy alias.

quantityMethodContract.unitMasonry: Unchanged ported math: ceil(height / (unitH + gap)) courses x ceil(segLen / (unitL + gap)) units; mortar bags ceil(sqft*2/30) x setting rate; production hours = units / setting bricks-per-hour.
quantityMethodContract.pouredConcrete: materialQuantity = (outlineLinearInches x wallHeightInches x wallThicknessInches) / 46656 in3-per-CY. No courses (numCourses 0), no mortar (mortarCost/bags 0), no production hours (laborHours 0 — there is no per-unit basis to divide by). Labor remains wall-face-area x $/sqft with the minimum charge. Internal fill: same CY method on the reduced inner run (closed outlines still subtract outer+inner thickness per corner).
quantityMethodContract.dimensionContract: Poured rows require exactly ONE cataloged dimension: wall_unit_width_inches read as wall thickness. Length/height are not consumed (noise/0s/malformed values there never hold a poured wall). Malformed/0/negative/missing thickness -> wall_unit_width_inches_unavailable hold.
quantityMethodContract.unitBasisContract: cost_per_unit on a poured row is $/CY. A blank/absent unit field keeps the implicit CY basis; recorded spellings cy/cyd/cy.d/yd/yd3/cu_yd/cubic yard(s)/yard(s) are accepted; ANY other recorded unit (each, sqft, bag, lf, ton, non-string) -> wall_material_unit_mismatch hold — never multiply cubic yards by a per-each price.
quantityMethodContract.subtypeUnavailable: A recorded subtype the alias table cannot resolve (glass_block, precast, adobe, 5, {}) -> wall_material_subtype_unavailable hold. Unknown families are never laundered to masonry and never guessed concrete.
quantityMethodContract.subtypePrecedence: The declared subtype picks the method over material_type — a legacy brick_stone row marked 'concrete' is poured (priced per CY on its thickness).
quantityMethodContract.consumedSettings: wall_labor_rate + wall_minimum_charge still consumed (area labor). wall_labor_bricks_per_hour is only validated when a unit-masonry path consumes it (masonry outer, or masonry fill under a poured outer). wall_mortar_cost_per_bag + mortar-gap drafts/overrides are only validated when a masonry side consumes them — malformed mortar settings no longer hold a fully-poured wall they cannot affect.
quantityMethodContract.overrides: custom_outer_material_qty on a poured row is a CY override (2 -> material cost = 2 x $/CY); explicit 0 stays a legitimate free/zero-material override; malformed -> held. Mortar qty/rate overrides are only checked on masonry sides.
quantityMethodContract.snapshot: calcWalls writes materialQuantityUnit: 'cy' (and internalMaterialQuantityUnit) onto calculatedCosts ONLY for poured rows — no new keys on masonry snapshots, so byte-level snapshot parity is preserved and the recorded basis rides acknowledged saves through holds untouched.

surfaceChanges.partSync.js: Wall Builder parts mirror the snapshot basis: unit 'cy' vs 'unit' from calculatedCosts.materialQuantityUnit / internalMaterialQuantityUnit.

deliberateNonChanges: calcWallCosts internal math for unit masonry is untouched — the ported course/pitch/mortar/labor formulas are identical; the only additions are isConcrete branches that bypass them.
calcWallCosts return shape unchanged — no new keys on its return object; the CY basis is written only in calcWalls' calculatedCosts snapshot layer so direct-call output parity holds.
foundationInputValidation.js untouched — it validates non-wall cost inputs (concrete overrides, cabinet prices); no wall/subtype logic lives there.

Held-wall architecture untouched — held() still preserves acknowledged calculatedCosts verbatim; available/issues contract and issue-object shape unchanged (new codes reuse the same add() shape so foundationWallCatalogIssues/calcProject catalogIssues flow works unmodified).
Entity schema untouched — FoundationInventory.jsonc already declares wall_material_subtype (brick/cinderblock/stone/concrete enum) and unit.
FoundationWallsPanel still renders the wall-level 'Mortar gap' input for concrete-material walls — cosmetic input, not consumed by the poured path; left as-is to keep the panel change minimal.
brick_stone rows keep legacy behavior: absent subtype = unit masonry; brick_* dims fill wall_unit_* at ingress exactly as O-008 established.
partSync's quantity fallback (|| 1) and all other part fields unchanged — only the unit label reads the recorded basis.
behaviorDeltas: Poured-concrete catalog rows become priceable: previously always held (UI preset wrote 0 unit length/height which failed the positive-dim check) or, with positive dims, priced a fictional unit count with mortar. Now they price placed volume in CY.
Recorded unrecognized subtype spellings now hold with wall_material_subtype_unavailable instead of silently pricing as unit masonry.
Poured rows with a recorded non-CY unit now hold with wall_material_unit_mismatch instead of multiplying CY by a per-each price.
Malformed bricks-per-hour/mortar settings no longer hold fully-poured walls that cannot consume them (still hold any masonry side).
calculatedCosts snapshots on poured walls carry materialQuantityUnit: 'cy' — consumed by BOM labels, panel display, and Builder part units.
Catalog writes: concrete preset saves unit 'cy' + null L/H; save coerces unit 'cy' on poured rows; masonry presets declare unit 'each'.

knownRemainders.savedSnapshotRepricing: Walls held under the OLD remote contract (0-dim concrete holds) retain their acknowledged saved costs until repriced — by design; the first successful price writes the CY snapshot.
knownRemainders.concreteForming: This scope covers wall-material catalog classification only; forming_material/rebar/ready-mix delivery surfaces are Phase B-2 concerns and untouched.
knownRemainders.panelMortarGapInput: The wall-level mortar-gap draft input still displays on poured-material walls (unconsumed, cosmetic) — a FoundationWallsPanel UX follow-up if product wants it hidden per selected subtype.
knownRemainders.offEnumAuthoredRows: Entity enum restricts subtype to the canonical four at the platform layer; off-enum rows can only arrive via direct entity writes/imports — the boundary holds them rather than guessing, which is the intended fail-closed posture.
